newsitem.title: New Zealand: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 1.

text.p: Morgan paid $56,000 since 'quitting' ATN: NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morga, who resigned as a director of Aotearoa Television Network on August 30 last year, was paid director's wages in September October and November, totalling $56,250. Page 1.
Youth Affairs Minister twice felt suicidal: Youth Affairs Minister Deborah Morris says she knows what it is like to feel suicidal. Page 1.
Kindergarten teachers protest at bill: A bill rammed through Parliament amid acrimonious debate and protest from the public gallery has angered kindergarten teachers. Page 2.

Japanese note attitude change: Prime Minister Jim Bolger had made a significant change in attitude by acknowledging the importance of an American presence in Asia, a senior official travelling with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Wednesday. Page 2.
Prebble taking Morgan case to police: ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble said on Wednesday night he was taking the latest Tuku Morgan disclosure involving a trip to Europe to police. Page 2.
Referendum 'likely to fail': The "appalling" management of the compulsory superannuation referendum meant it would almost certainly fail, said ACT NZ superannuation spokesman Ken Shirley. Page 2.

Jobs will go, says Douglas: Council of Trade Unions president Ken Douglas on Wednesday warned of "big-time" job losses if the government continued to "deregulate, privatise and reduce government functions." Page 2.

Millions offered after MAF computer glitch: The government is to set up a $10 million compensation fund for fishermen affected by a 10-year-old computer glitch in the quota management system operated by the Agriculture and Fisheries Ministry. Page 9.

AMP considers pursuing role as fully licensed bank: AMP New Zealand's phone banking arm Ergo should have a $1 billion home loan portfolio by the end of the year and the group might seek a full banking licence soon, general manager Rodney Cook said on Wednesday. Page 11.

Savers will be able to have a choice on whether to use existing savings to meet contributions required by the proposed compulsory superannuation programme, Treasurer Winston Peters said on Wednesday. Page 11.

Reserve Bank urged to ease conditions: Recent surveys showing business pessimism, coupled with low inflation figures, have caused a sea-change in some economists' inflation outlook and they want the Reserve Bank to ease monetary conditions now. Page 11.
Nutricia purchase: Auckland-based Nutricia Australasia has acquired the Robinsons brand of baby cereals, giving it a 50 percent share of the baby cereal market in New Zealand. Page 11.
